price_per_million.source: copied from reasoning_models_v1 (confirmed 2026-11-11); thinking tokens billed as output

methodological_questions: Can a teammate DRIVE be identified and sequenced before a PNR reliably, given inferred play-type labels?
Is any PPP difference causal or confounded by player quality, lineup, defense and score and clock context?
Does label construction (foul leakage, outcome-dependent flags, proxy-calibrated PNR labels) create or mask a PPP difference?
How many drive-then-PNR possessions exist per cell, and is there power for a pooled test?
Does a placebo comparison remove the apparent premium?

historical_evidence.finding: Descriptive same-initiator and teammate sequence premiums. DRIVE->PNR cells were mixed: L. Doncic DRIVE->PNR +0.309 (n=53), D. Bane DRIVE->PNR -0.324 (n=70, t=-2.7), and J. Brown->J. Tatum DRIVE->PNR +0.326 (n=43). The Brown->Tatum result was later shown to be a placebo artifact (APPS-070). Minimum n=30 per cell, no multiplicity correction, mixed signs on the same pair across players. Recorded validation status: same_pipeline_validation.
Label backfill verification overall FAIL. PNR share 28.7% (band 20-28%), 3100 games with team PNR >33%, team identity FAIL, 82.8% of PNR labels proxy_calibrated. PNR PPP 0.948 passed.
Play-type label audit FAIL: OTHER 20.2%, 40.8% low confidence, DRIVE foul-draw 1.7% vs 14-22% benchmark, foul possessions leak into OTHER. Recorded limits: label error, leakage, small sample.
DRIVE foul rate sits 12pp below benchmark; PNR shows a 22% foul rate; only 0.7% of possessions map to a real play type via initiation_type.
An assisted flag existing only on makes produced SPOT_UP 2.83 PPP; fixed by rewriting the inferrer (SPOT_UP ~1.16).
PBP shot-level PNR rates vary by team (OKC 7.6% to IND 13.8%); this is a calibration input for the proxy PNR labeler, with no pass/fail gate.
PNR possession share rose +12.1pp from RS to playoffs, which may reflect tagging differences. Recorded risks: label error, mechanical floor.
Team-level PNR PPP was 0.173 lower in playoffs than RS (25 teams, no CIs), so RS and playoff PNR PPP are not exchangeable.

Playoff series game buckets: PNR PPP +0.087 across the series, with regression-to-the-mean and selection caveats and no CIs. This is a drift signal rather than evidence on the drive-before-PNR question.
On-ball coverage labels were unusable (labeled 14.9% and 3.3% of possessions; switches_on unpopulated). The defensive-scheme covariate is therefore not available.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Cell-level teammate sequence premiums (min n=30) read as signal, including DRIVE->PNR.
failed_approaches.why: Small cells, no multiplicity correction, mixed signs, and the Brown->Tatum cell was shown to be a placebo artifact (APPS-070).
Distribution and identity checks failed; mostly proxy-calibrated PNR labels; label error.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Inferred play-type labels used as clean measures of DRIVE and PNR.
failed_approaches.why: Systematic label error, foul leakage and a low-confidence share.

failed_approaches.what_failed: PPP comparisons by play type without separating foul endings.
failed_approaches.why: Foul-ending leakage and a poor initiation_type mapping created artifacts.

failed_approaches.what_failed: A classifier feature available only on makes.
failed_approaches.why: Outcome-derived leakage produced fake PPP; a similar construction could affect PNR labels.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Labeling on-ball coverage from matchup and PBP fields.

evidence_establishes: No retrieved record tests the pooled hypothesis that any teammate DRIVE preceding a PNR raises PNR PPP; the closest evidence (FAM:SF40) is descriptive.
In FAM:SF40, DRIVE->PNR cell-level premiums have mixed signs (+0.309 Doncic, -0.324 Bane), and the one teammate positive example (Brown->Tatum) was shown to be a placebo artifact.
Per the recorded audits, the derived play-type labels, including PNR and DRIVE, carry label error, foul leakage and proxy calibration, so PNR PPP and the DRIVE label are measured with known error.
Recorded RS vs playoff differences (PNR PPP -0.173 and +12.1pp share) show that PNR PPP and labeling are not stable across contexts.
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether a pooled average effect of a teammate drive on subsequent PNR PPP exists or is zero.
The size of any effect after adjustment for ball-handler, screener, lineup, opponent, score and clock.
How label error in DRIVE or PNR would bias a pooled estimate; no record gives validated precision or recall for the DRIVE->PNR sequence.
How many qualifying drive-then-PNR possessions exist in the 2022-26 data, and any placebo-adjusted pooled estimate.
own_inferences: The unqualified word 'any' makes the claim a universal; a pooled average effect is the only testable reading, and it can be tested in the sense of estimating the average, not every pairing.

A naive comparison of PNR PPP after a drive vs without will probably show a difference because of selection: drives happen in particular possession states (early clock, transition-ish, attacked defense), and the labeler likely classifies those states differently.

Possession-level sequencing may be mechanically linked: a drive that ends in a kickout then PNR, or a foul in the sequence, changes what gets labeled PNR and how it ends, so the contrast is partly constructed by the labeler.
The most likely outcome of a competent test is a small, label-sensitive, placebo-sensitive pooled effect, which would be hard to separate from artifact.
uncertainties: The recorded audits cover earlier label versions; the current labeler state and validated accuracy for DRIVE and PNR are unknown.
Whether the sequence is within the same possession and how the 'preceding' window is defined (t-1, t-2, or time) is not specified in the question.
The number of qualifying possessions, and the share of those with a high-confidence label, are unknown.
APPS-070 (the placebo study) was not itself retrieved, so its design is known only through the FAM:SF40 note.
2025-26 playoff data are partial before 2026-06-21; the question was posed on 2026-06-14.

historical_effect.explanation: Without history I would have proceeded with a straightforward contrast. The retrieved records show that PNR and DRIVE labels fail audits, that outcome-derived or foul-related label leakage has already produced artifacts, and that a teammate DRIVE->PNR premium (Brown->Tatum) turned out to be a placebo artifact. This moved the decision to proceed_with_changes: reframe to a pooled, label-validated, placebo-controlled estimate with a pre-specified exclusion of foul-ending and low-confidence labels.

blocking_constraints.text: Both the DRIVE and PNR labels are inferred, failed prior audits, and are mostly proxy-calibrated; a pooled effect is not interpretable unless the sequence is validated.
Labeling features that depend on outcomes (assisted flag, fouls) can link the drive label and the PNR PPP mechanically.
A prior teammate DRIVE->PNR premium disappeared under placebo; a result without a placebo comparison is not credible.

prior_work.summary: Only descriptive cell-level DRIVE->PNR premiums exist (mixed signs, no multiplicity correction, one placebo artifact). No pooled, adjusted test of the question has been retrieved. Label audits failed.

risks.text: DRIVE and PNR are inferred; audits show systematic error, a high low-confidence share and proxy-calibrated PNR. Misclassification of the preceding action and of the PNR is likely non-random.
Foul and assisted-flag leakage into labels (SF-PAP-096, SF-CHT-025) may make the label depend on the possession outcome.
Drive-preceded PNRs differ in ball-handler, screener, lineup, opponent, clock, score and defensive state; defensive coverage is not labelable (SF-APPS-058).
Brown->Tatum DRIVE->PNR was a placebo artifact; the test needs shuffled or pseudo-sequence placebos.
Cell-level n of 30-70 gives low power; the pooled version is feasible only if enough high-confidence drive-then-PNR possessions exist.
Prior work flagged cells at |t|>=2 with no correction; subgroup mining by player pair must be avoided or corrected.
The 'preceding' action must be defined by clock before the PNR starts, and the PNR label must not use information from after the drive's outcome.
RS vs playoff PNR PPP and tagging differ (SF-APPS-011, SF-APPS-012); pooling across seasons and phases needs stratification.
Selecting teams or players with high-drive volume or high PPP invites regression to the mean.

design.estimand: Average difference in PNR PPP (points per possession) between PNR possessions preceded by a teammate DRIVE (different initiator than the PNR ball-handler, within a pre-registered window, e.g. same possession and the prior 8 seconds) and matched PNR possessions with no preceding drive, adjusted for context; compared against a placebo preceding action (e.g. a non-drive teammate action of similar timing). Primary statement is a pooled average treatment-like contrast, not any individual pairing.
design.unit: Half-court PNR possession (excluding possessions where the PNR label is low-confidence and possessions ending in fouls handled via a separate sensitivity analysis), clustered by game/team.
design.sample: 2022-23 through 2024-25 regular seasons and playoffs as the discovery set, with 2025-26 regular season (complete) as a pre-registered holdout, playoffs analyzed separately; the 2025-26 playoffs are excluded until complete (2026-06-21). Only high-confidence labels after manual validation of a random sample (e.g. 300 sequences) to estimate precision of the drive-then-PNR label.
design.power: Before looking at outcomes, count qualifying possessions per season. Require at least ~2,000 treated and 8,000 control possessions for the pooled test; with PPP SD about 1.1-1.2, this detects roughly 0.06-0.07 PPP at 80% power. If counts or label precision fall below the thresholds (e.g. validated precision <85%), declare untestable rather than test.
design.controls: Mixed model or matched design with ball-handler and screener fixed or random effects, lineup/team and opponent, season, phase (RS vs playoffs), period, clock at PNR start, score margin, transition vs half-court, and prior possession type. Sensitivity: exclude foul-ending possessions and recompute using shot-quality (PPP excluding fouls) and eFG-like outcomes. Label audit stratification by proxy_calibrated vs direct labels.
design.falsification: Placebo: replace the drive with other teammate actions (CUT, SPOT_UP, hand-off) and with shuffled actions from other possessions of the same team/game; the drive effect must exceed the placebo distribution. Negative control: effect on the drive-preceded possessions' outcome when the PNR label is permuted. Replicate in the holdout without refitting. Check that the effect is not present in cases where the labeler used outcome-derived features.
design.multiplicity: One pre-registered primary test (pooled effect, two-sided, alpha 0.05). Season, phase and label-confidence subgroups are secondary and Holm-corrected; no player-pair or team-level mining. Player-level heterogeneity is reported only as variance, not cell-by-cell significance.
design.decision_rule: Supported only if the pooled adjusted effect is positive with the 95% CI excluding zero in discovery and the same sign and CI excluding zero in the holdout, it exceeds the placebo distribution, and it survives the foul-excluded and high-confidence-label sensitivity analyses. Rejected if the CI lies within about ±0.03 PPP with adequate power. Artifact if the effect disappears under placebo or label-confidence restriction. Untestable if validated label precision or sample thresholds fail.
design.data_version: NBA stats API per-game files and the derived play-type possession graph as of 2026-06-14: seasons 2022-23 to 2024-25 complete, 2025-26 regular season complete, 2025-26 playoffs partial and excluded; record the labeler code version and hash before analysis.

methodological_questions: Can a drive be identified and sequenced before a PNR from play-by-play data reliably?
Does a preceding teammate drive causally raise PNR PPP or is it confounded by lineup, player quality and possession context?
How does play-type label error or derived-label dependence on outcomes affect PPP estimates?
What sample size and exposure frequency exist for drive-then-PNR possessions?
Which controls and placebo comparisons were used in earlier action-sequencing studies?
args.query: teammate drive before pick-and-roll effect on PNR points per possession; play-type labeling and data quality

system_prompt:
You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.
- search_documents(query): rank further study-family documents by text relevance; returns up to 10 families not yet returned.
- read_family(id): the complete record of one study family (for example 'FAM:SF-APPA-001').

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY

Research question (as posed on 2026-06-14, in the area of play-type labeling and data quality):
Any teammate DRIVE preceding a PNR raises PNR PPP.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

Stage 1. Reply only with the retrieval call: {"action": "tool", "tool": "retrieve_history", "args": {"research_concepts": ["..."], "methodological_questions": ["..."], "query": "..."}}
